reviewed: English concept sections, embedded lab code and recorded outputs
Worked examples, exercise solutions, quizzes and guided reading
Consistency of claims across concepts, labs and exercises
Widget source calculations and bilingual labels
scope.method: Read-only source inspection, manual reasoning and primary-source documentation checks.
limitations: Recorded lab outputs were inspected rather than rerun during this review.
This review does not establish runtime behaviour, browser layout or accessibility.
The Chinese prose and page metadata for Modules 6-8 remain to be produced and reviewed.
Translation and publication are paused following the user's instruction to review without running code.

findings.title: Count both input biases for biased SwiGLU
findings.evidence: The generic parameter counter supports glu=True and bias='all', but adds only d_ff + d FFN bias parameters. SwiGLU has two d-to-d_ff projections and one d_ff-to-d projection, requiring 2*d_ff + d biases per layer.
findings.impact: This supported configuration silently undercounts parameters by L*d_ff. The listed reference configurations do not exercise the combination, so their successful comparisons would not reveal the error.
findings.recommendation: Replace the bias contribution with (2 if cfg.glu else 1) * cfg.d_ff + cfg.d. When execution is allowed again, compare this configuration against a corresponding instantiated model.

findings.title: Make few-shot troubleshooting match the recorded experiment
findings.evidence: The paragraph attributes a roughly 20-point accuracy swing to reordering the same examples and says predictions follow the last labels. Lab 4 records AABB accuracy 0.6250 and BBAA 0.6875, a 6.25-point order difference. Their A prediction fractions are 0.8750 and 0.3125 respectively, opposite simple attraction to the final label. The 18.75-point accuracy spread belongs to different eight-shot example selections.
findings.impact: Learners are directed to diagnose recency bias from an experiment that does not support it. Exercise 8 already explains this correctly, creating an internal contradiction.
findings.recommendation: Separate example-selection sensitivity from order sensitivity, use the recorded differences, and describe label-frequency effects without claiming their mechanism has been identified.

findings.title: Describe E=1.69 as a fitted asymptote
findings.evidence: The check answer calls E the loss no model can beat and says a perfect model would have perplexity exp(1.69). Section 1 and Exercise 7 correctly state that the fit does not prove the true source entropy equals 1.69.
findings.impact: The answer turns an empirical model's fitted parameter into a universal lower bound, overstating what the fit establishes.
findings.recommendation: Say the fitted law tends to 1.69 nats/token, corresponding to perplexity about 5.4 under that extrapolation. Preserve the caveat that this is not proof of the corpus's exact entropy, and make the Section 4 parameter description agree.

findings.title: Distinguish fp16 subnormal spacing, rounding and flushing
findings.evidence: The check answer says fp16 flushes values below about 6e-8 to zero. Its least positive subnormal is 2^-24, approximately 5.96e-8; with gradual underflow and round-to-nearest, values above half that spacing can round to a nonzero subnormal. For example, 4e-8 can round to 5.96e-8. Kernel-specific flushing is a separate behaviour. The section body already makes these distinctions.
findings.impact: The answer teaches the wrong universal zero threshold and contradicts the more precise explanation above it.
findings.recommendation: Make the answer agree with the body: values below half the least subnormal round to zero under round-to-nearest; some operations additionally flush subnormals.

findings.title: State view's stride condition rather than requiring global contiguity
findings.evidence: The prose and its check answer say view works only on contiguous memory. PyTorch allows views of noncontiguous tensors when the requested dimensions satisfy its size/stride compatibility condition. Merging the transposed head dimensions in this example does require a copy in the ordinary nondegenerate shape, but the general rule is broader.
findings.impact: Learners acquire an incorrect rule for reasoning about tensor layout and copies.
findings.recommendation: Explain that this head merge violates view's stride compatibility condition, and that reshape returns a view when possible and otherwise copies.

findings.title: Avoid guaranteeing post-norm divergence without warmup
findings.evidence: The passage says a post-norm model trained at its full learning rate from step one therefore diverges, followed by a general claim that pre-norm trains with little or no warmup. The cited paper establishes a mechanism for instability at large learning rates and demonstrates successful pre-norm recipes without warmup; it does not establish inevitable divergence for every post-norm recipe.
findings.impact: An empirical and recipe-dependent stability result becomes a universal claim.
findings.recommendation: Use 'can become unstable at a large learning rate' and say pre-norm often reduces warmup requirements. Keep learning rate, depth, initialization and the rest of the recipe relevant to the claim.

findings.title: Require exact verification for the false-candidate correctness claim
findings.evidence: The passage allows verification by either exact shingle Jaccard or the fraction of agreeing signature entries, then says false candidates cost time rather than correctness. Signature agreement is a random estimate and can accept a pair whose exact similarity is below the threshold.
findings.impact: Learners may substitute approximate verification while assuming it prevents erroneous removals.
findings.recommendation: Reserve the correctness claim for exact threshold verification under the declared clustering policy. If approximate signature verification is offered, describe its false-positive uncertainty. Lab 1 already uses exact word-shingle verification.

findings.title: Limit Chinese cost ratios to the measured text and separate latency assumptions
findings.evidence: A single bilingual paragraph's tokenizer ratios are extrapolated to all input and output text, to decode time by the same factor, and to a claim that a bilingual tokenizer keeps Chinese at or below English cost. Token ratios depend on the corpus. Decode step costs also depend on context length, KV traffic, batching and hardware.
findings.impact: The case-study budget reads as a guaranteed language and latency relationship rather than a conditional estimate.
findings.recommendation: Label the numbers as a scenario using the measured paragraph's ratios. Calculate billing under an explicit equal-rate assumption and treat decode latency as approximate only under fixed per-token throughput. Recommend measuring representative bilingual inputs and outputs.

findings.title: Repair literal question marks in guided-reading punctuation
findings.evidence: Two linked paper titles contain literal question marks where quotes belong, and the reading instruction says 'Sections 1?3'. These remain present when the file is read as UTF-8.
findings.impact: The published reading list would contain visible punctuation corruption.
findings.recommendation: Restore ordinary quotation marks and the intended range dash. Do not globally replace question marks, which are valid elsewhere in the module.
